title: Augustine of Hippo Born — Future Foundational Demonologist
description: Augustine of Hippo was born on November 13, 354 CE in Thagaste, Numidia (modern Algeria). Over the course of his life he would develop the most influential Christian demonological framework of antiquity, addressing questions of demonic reality, the capacity of demons to intervene in human affairs, and the epistemological status of apparent demonic miracles. His Confessions, The City of God, and numerous other works would together constitute the foundational Christian theological engagement with the demonic that shaped all subsequent medieval and early modern demonology. His treatment of the succubus/incubus tradition, demonic pacts, and the limits of demonic power became required reading for later witch-theorists.
historiographical_note: Stuart Clark's Thinking with Demons treats Augustine as the single most important patristic source for early modern demonological thinking, his framework on demonic illusion versus reality being particularly central to the debates within early modern witch theory.
source_method: Published scholarship; standard biographical sources; Clark, Thinking with Demons
